```{r setup}
library(controlcompR)
```

## Simulation with arbitrary inputs

`ctrl_simulate()` integrates a continuous model exactly for inputs that
are piecewise constant (zero-order hold, the default) or piecewise linear
(first-order hold) between the time points, using matrix exponentials of
augmented matrices. No numerical ODE solver is involved, so the result is
exact up to rounding:

```{r}
sys <- ctrl_ss(matrix(c(0, 1, -4, -0.8), 2, byrow = TRUE), c(0, 1), c(1, 0))
t <- seq(0, 15, by = 0.05)
u <- as.numeric(t > 1) - as.numeric(t > 6)
res <- ctrl_simulate(sys, input = u, times = t)
plot(res)
head(as.data.frame(res))
```

For a discrete model the simulation is the difference equation itself and
`times` must be multiples of the sample interval.

## Step, impulse and initial-condition responses

When no time grid is given, one is chosen from the slowest and fastest
poles. Each input is applied in turn:

```{r}
mimo <- ctrl_ss(diag(c(-1, -3)), matrix(c(1, 0.5, 0, 1), 2), diag(2))
plot(ctrl_step(mimo))
plot(ctrl_impulse(sys))
plot(ctrl_initial(sys, x0 = c(1, 0)))
```

## Step characteristics

```{r}
G <- ctrl_tf(9, c(1, 1.2, 9))
info <- ctrl_step_info(G)
info
```

The definitions are explicit: rise time from 10 to 90 percent of the final
change, settling time as the last exit from a 2 percent band, overshoot
and undershoot as percentages of the final change. For a stable model the
final value is taken from the DC gain; otherwise the last simulated sample
is used and `settled` says whether the response had stopped changing. The
classical approximation for the overshoot of a second order system,
\(100 e^{-\pi \zeta / \sqrt{1 - \zeta^2}}\), agrees:

```{r}
zeta <- 1.2 / (2 * 3)
100 * exp(-pi * zeta / sqrt(1 - zeta^2))
```

## Integral performance criteria

`ctrl_performance()` computes IAE, ISE, ITAE, RMSE, control effort and the
largest bound violation for any recorded experiment:

```{r}
st <- ctrl_step(G)
ctrl_performance(st$time, st$y[, 1, 1], r = 1)
```
